# 周易口訣義

**ID:** KR1a0009
**Custom ID:** ZB1a0008
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V8.1, p1
**Extent:** 6 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 史徵 (唐朝) 撰

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A six-*juàn* Táng *Yì* commentary by [史徵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E5%BE%B5) Shǐ Zhēng of Hénán, presented in the form of explanatory expansions of mnemonic verses (*kǒujué* 口訣) — short summary formulae used in classroom-style oral instruction. The author's preface frames the project as a deliberate simplification: "Taking [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng's note as primary and condensing [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) Kǒng's sub-commentary as governing principle" (*xiān yǐ Wáng zhù wéi zōng, hòu yuē Kǒng shū wéi lǐ* 先以王注為宗，後約孔疏為理). The hexagram-statements (*tuàn* 彖) and line-statements (*yáo*) are commented in full; the *Tuàn zhuàn* commentary on hexagrams is in some places cut short. The work is divided into upper and lower canon, and named "*kǒujué*" — "mnemonic verse" — because the *yì jué* 義決 ("decisive meaning") is treated as its operative idiom.

Eight hexagrams are missing in transmission — 豫 Yù, 隨 Suí, 无妄 Wúwàng, 大壯 Dàzhuàng, 晉 Jìn, 睽 Kuí, 蹇 Jiǎn, 解 Xiè, and 中孚 Zhōngfú (the Sìkù *tiyao*'s tally of "eight" appears slightly miscounted; nine hexagrams are listed) — but the Sìkù editors decided to retain the original six-*juàn* division.

The catalog dynasty is Táng. The Sìkù editors' adjudication, against Sòng-period confusions that recorded the author variously as 史證 / 史文徽 / 史之徴 (taboo-avoidance and graphic-confusion variants), follows the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* 永樂大典 and [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) Zhū Yízūn's *Jīngyì kǎo* in fixing the form 史徴 and the dynasty as Táng. The composition window 700–900 reflects the broad Táng span that the present evidence supports; tighter dating is not currently defensible (the work cites [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò's pool of pre-Táng commentators but is not securely placed within the Táng century).

**Abstract**

[史徵](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%B2%E5%BE%B5) Shǐ Zhēng of Hénán 河南 (the Tang superior prefecture corresponding to modern Luòyáng) is a poorly documented mid-to-late Táng *Yì* scholar — present in the bibliographic record but not in the *Tángshū liè zhuàn*, with no surviving inscription. The graph of his given name (*zhēng* 徴 / 證 / 徽) was unstable in transmission; the Sìkù editors, following the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* and [朱彝尊](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9C%B1%E5%BD%9D%E5%B0%8A) Zhū Yízūn, fix the form 史徴 and the dynasty as Táng (against [陳振孫](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B3%E6%8C%AF%E5%AD%AB) Chén Zhènsūn's "Táng or Five Dynasties").

The *kǒujué* 口訣 ("mnemonic verse") format reflects a Táng didactic tradition of distillation-into-formulae for classroom recitation; the present work is the only example of the genre to survive in the *Yì*-commentary corpus, although analogous works existed for the *Sānlǐ* and *Chūnqiū* traditions in [陸德明](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E5%BE%B7%E6%98%8E) Lù Démíng's bibliography. Shǐ Zhēng's preface explicitly subordinates the project to [王弼](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BC%BC) Wáng Bì's note and [孔穎達](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AD%94%E7%A9%8E%E9%81%94) Kǒng Yǐngdá's *zhèngyì* — but, as the Sìkù editors document at length, his actual commentary draws extensively on a pool of pre-Táng masters whose works were already lost in the Sòng (Master Zhōu 周氏, Master Lǐ 李氏, Master Zhuāng 莊氏, Master Zhāng 張氏, Master Chǔ 褚氏, [鄭眾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%84%AD%E7%9C%BE) Zhèng Zhòng, [王廙](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%8B%E5%BB%99) Wáng Yì, [宋衷](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AE%8B%E8%A1%B7) Sòng Zhōng, [何妥](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%95%E5%A6%A5) Hé Tuǒ, [周弘正](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%91%A8%E5%BC%98%E6%AD%A3) Zhōu Hóngzhèng, [侯果](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BE%AF%E6%9E%9C) Hóu Guǒ, [虞翻](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%99%9E%E7%BF%BB) Yú Fān, [荀爽](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8D%80%E7%88%BD) Xún Shuǎng, [陸績](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%99%B8%E7%B8%BE) Lù Jì). For several of these, Shǐ Zhēng's quotations are now the sole surviving witness; for others (Yú Fān at *Kǎn* upper-six, Xún Shuǎng at the *Yí* *Dàxiàng*, Wáng Yì at the *Bì* *Dàxiàng*) his text is substantively independent of and richer than the parallel [李鼎祚](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E9%BC%8E%E7%A5%9A) Lǐ Dǐngzuò *Jíjiě* witness.

The Sìkù editors place Shǐ Zhēng's book on a list of five surviving pre-Sòng *Yì* commentaries — [京房](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BA%AC%E6%88%BF) Jīng Fáng's *Yìzhuàn* [KR1a0166](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0166), Wáng Bì [KR1a0006](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0006), Kǒng Yǐngdá [KR1a0007](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0007), Lǐ Dǐngzuò [KR1a0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0008), and the present work — and explicitly note that the great Qīng evidential reconstructors ([惠棟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%83%A0%E6%A3%9F) Huì Dòng's *Jiǔjīng gǔyì*, [余蕭客](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E4%BD%99%E8%95%AD%E5%AE%A2) Yú Xiāokè's *Gǔ jīng jiě gōuchén*) had overlooked it. The discovery within the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* material brought it back into critical view in the Sìkù period.

The transmitted text in the *Yǒnglè dàdiǎn* lacks eight hexagrams in their entirety (per the Sìkù tally; nine hexagrams are listed and the discrepancy is unresolved); the surviving fifty-six-or-fifty-five-hexagram text was issued in six *juàn* in the Sìkù WYG.
